ducing the summer and fall spores

Do you believe in signs? We do sometime. When street kid sticks his thumb to his nose and wiggles his fingers, it's a sign. It means something. When the pee pee (petersburg press) explodes it. self on a nest fouling blast, we have a hunch that it's sign. We are taking up~ the article in last weeks whirl of the pee-pee on the strength of a sign. By inuendo and yelled, roundabout assertion we opine that the screed is meant for THE AL ASKAN. The shoe doesn't fit us at all. In fact we can't imagine that it would fit anybody, but since we feel that there is an allusion to us we'll go ahead. However, we'll play fairer, we won't leave anything to the imagination. If we mean the pee-pee we'll say so. It is ev- ident that the pee-pee didn't have the sand, gumption, guts or some thing to come out openly and above board in it's harangue. and Marriage


The average woman likes to believe that the man she marries is strong enough and capable enough to support her, protect her and in necessary in an emergency, not tyrannize over her. In other words, she likes to look UP TO the man she has chosen as a life-partner.


Nothing is more maddening, more heart-breaking to a wife than to discover that the man she married cannot live up in all respects to his position as head of the family.


Dear Miss Fairfax, " writes Fay on this theme. Please tell me what to do. My husband is a failure, a total loss.


He is a dreamer. We've been married five years and have two darling baby boys but that's all. I have no future, no hopes, no friends, no social life, just stay at home day in and day out with nothing to do but wash and take care of the babies. No home of my own either, just 4 rooms at his mother's, never have a dime and what the children have is given to them.


Before the children came, I had a good position and things were a little better, for I could at least pay my own way. But now with the babies, I feel so helpless. My poor old father-in-law has a wife with a small salary to support. This has gone on for over five years. My husband is a dreamer, who does I try to make his dreams come true. He has had a number of good jobs since we were married. At first he is always enthusiastic. But soon he loses all interest, finds something wrong with the boss or some of his fellow workers, and eventually loses his job or quits.


Finally, he decided to go in business for himself. So he borrowed all the money he could, went into debt to the entire town and started a small cafe.


He worked earnestly for a while and I had hopes. I even jumped in and waited on tables. But now he has lost all interest. He doesn't keep it clean and attractive and has lost most of his customers.


Why in the name of peace can't he retake his foothold? He isn't a dumb bell, he has brains. What can I do to help him? Among his friends he is a good fellow. He will close his business almost any afternoon and go out for a game of ball with the boys. He will lend any of them his last dollar.


He shows me perfect fidelity, is a lovable man, but a failure. This can't go on forever. All but when I think of how he has thrown me on his parents, I almost hate him. Don't tell me to try to make a success for my sake, please solve my problem.


Gladly I will help you if I can, Fay. Your husband is one of those lovable, impracticable dreamers who have been the joy and despair of wives since time began.


Of course, you love him. OF COURSE YOU want to help him. You have one chance of saving the situation, just a slender chance, which will call for all your heroism. You will have to rise to the occasion and become head of the family if you are to hold your little home together. Your husband is not a failure as a husband, but only as a money-maker. You, I am sure, possess the practical business spirit he lacks. Use it, save his business for him.


Even though you may have to hire a woman to take charge of the children part of each day to relieve their grandmother, that will be worth while if you can retrieve and build up the cafe and make enough to take care of yourself and the children and pay for a nurse for them.


Go about this venture tactfully. Explain to your husband your longing for a career and desire to go into partnership with him in managing the cafe. Then see that the cafe is the most attractive, the cleanest in town, and serves the best food. You can do this I am sure and you have every incentive. It will be hard to head the business and the family without fatally wounding the pride of your husband, but if you are clever YOU can do this and let him think he is head, not merely assistant.


If you prefer, take jobs to make your living or hire a nursemaid for the children and go back to your business position and make a success. You and your children must live. You cannot be a charitable burden on feeble old age without losing all respect for yourself.


I do not advise the average wife to support her husband. I certainly would warn every girl against marrying a man who cannot or will not take care of her.


But you have a husband whom you love and who is a financial failure. If you will rise to the occasion, will it not be possible to bring out all your own innate ability and save your marriage and home?

cardboard box. She could tell that it was

cheer of the luncheon table

The Luther League of North Gros- veordale have been notified that the New England Luther League will hold their annual league conference at Webster Lake during the month of August and the first week of Septem- Der. Many cottages at kildeer Island have been leased for the period of the conference. The community house on the island will be used as a meet ing place for conferences to be held during the time that the members will be present.

 During the session, a well known Augustanna College professor will be in charge of the meetings, assisted by numerous ministers of the New Eng land Conference.

 Eighty four churches with sixty-six societies and fifty-four pastors are re- presented in the conference which also includes four districts, those of Boston, Hartford. Worcester and Providence.

 The executive committee in charge of the arrangements of the vacation camp are: Rev. Peter Froeberg, Brockton; Hon. Joseph L. Larson, Ev- erett; Rev. Nore Gustafson, Stamford, Conn, Rev. Frank s. Granquist, Pom tiae, K. l.; Adolph Luthgren of Spring field, Mass; Miss Helga E. Peterson of Worcester Mass; Miss Helen E. Range of North Easton, Mass.

 Many members of the Swedish Luther League are planning to at tend this conference. Undoubtedly, this conference will be the largest ever held since 1t is centrally located for all districts.
